Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back. Andy Balbirnie leads his men out on the park. Out walk the two Bangladeshi openers, Shadman Islam and Mahmudul Hasan Joy. Jordan Neill will start the attack for Ireland. Here we go!
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Right then, as expected, Bangladesh have opted against enforcing the follow-on. The way Ireland batted will certainly make Shanto and Co. think about their declaration, as they will need to leave themselves enough time to bowl the visitors out in the second innings. Ireland, meanwhile, will be on the hunt for early wickets as they look to make a mark with the ball and challenge the home side. Back in a bit for Bangladesh's second innings.

After Doheny’s dismissal, Tucker carried on the good work alongside Jordan Neill, but much like Doheny, Neill fell against the run of play as the second new ball brought Bangladesh success. Lorcan Tucker continued to show trust in the tail as Ireland looked to chip away at the deficit, but they eventually folded for 265. Taijul Islam was the pick of the bowlers with four wickets, and apart from Mominul Haque, every bowler used chipped in with at least one.

Bangladesh end up with a significant lead of 211 runs, and although they have the option of enforcing the follow-on, it doesn’t look like they will, given that they have already been in the field for 88.3 overs. Najmul Hossain Shanto's side were made to work hard, especially today, due to a spirited fightback from Ireland. It looked worrying for the tourists at 94/5, but what followed was a steady recovery built around Lorcan Tucker. The way Tucker and Stephen Doheny began the day was particularly pleasing from an Irish perspective, as they took a positive approach against the Bangladesh spinners.

Taijul Islam removed Stephen Doheny and Andy McBrine in the space of three balls to pull things back but since then Jordan Neill has partnered with Lorcan Tucker to stitch yet another partnership. These two have played the spinners well but there's a mountain to climb for the Irish team. They need the next session to go their way as well but Bangladesh will try and correct themselves to get a healthy first innings lead. Stay tuned for the second session, which will begin at 6.10 am GMT.

A proactive batting display from Ireland have helped them start Day 3 on a superb note. Excellent batting from the Irish team. Although they lost 2 wickets in the session, they have scored 113 runs. Stephen Doheny and Lorcan Tucker were coming into Day 3 under a bit of pressure as Ireland were 98/5. However, some inconsistent bowling saw Ireland take their chances and score a fruitful haul of boundaries. The 81-run stand between Stephen Doheny and Lorcan Tucker settled things before the earthquake arrived here in Dhaka. Literally.

They will have to believe that it is a matter of one mistake from either of the two batters, and who knows, they can get on a roll from there.

Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to get going on Day 3. The two umpires and players head out to the middle. It is another lovely morning in Mirpur. Bangladesh are starting with spin in the form of Taijul Islam. Lorcan Tucker to face the first ball. Two slips and a short leg in place. Here we go!

PITCH REPORT - Isobel Joyce is down by the deck. She says the Irish batters will have to show conviction and take a leaf out of Bangladesh's batters when they come out to bat today. Mentions that the Irish batters didn't come forward much, and they paid the price for it. Shares that a major difference between the spinners of the two sides was how slow Bangladesh's spin attack bowled. Adds that the Bangladesh bowlers need to bowl the same way, and they'll pick up wickets.

Ireland's Gavin Hoey is also up for a chat. He says a Test debut is always special, and his dad, who has also represented Ireland, is just as proud. Mentions that with plenty of experience in the playing group, and having played club cricket with some of the guys, settling in was easy, as the team passed on valuable insights. Hoey feels he bowled better on Day 1 but got the rewards on Day 2. Believes that sending down 34 overs against a solid batting unit that plays spin well will hold him in good stead moving forward.

Litton Das is up for a quick chat. He says it's a special feeling whenever he scores a century. Reckons he feels lucky to play a part in Rahim's 100th Test match. Adds that he has experience throughout his entire career and is a cool and calm guy. Tells that it was a bit difficult in the last game as he didn't play red-ball cricket recently, but practised a lot and that helped him approach better in this game.

It is not going to get any easier for Ireland, with half the side already back in the hut. They still have Andy McBrine and Jordan Neill to come, both of whom showed promise in Sylhet, but the challenge here will be far sterner with the surface expected to wear further. For the visitors, it will be all about building partnerships and digging deep. Stick around for what promises to be another entertaining day.

Day 2 saw Mushfiqur Rahim, playing in his 100th Test, and Litton Das complete their centuries. Bangladesh looked on course to breach the 500-run mark but eventually finished with a formidable 476. With the ball, while the pacers were inconsistent, the spinners were anything but. There was noticeably more turn on offer compared to the opening day, especially in the final session. Whether that was down to the skill set of the Bangladesh spinners or the surface beginning to wear, perhaps a bit of both, it certainly made life challenging for the Irish batters.

Hello, one and all! Day 3 is upon us at the Shere Bangla National Stadium. It has been two strong days for Bangladesh, who find themselves firmly in control of the Test. For Ireland, apart from the opening session of the match, little has gone their way. They will need to show the stomach for a fight, or else the game might drift even further away from them by the end of this all-important ‘Moving Day’.
... DAY 3, SESSION 1 ...

The Irish batters are in all sorts of trouble, and we feel it's going to get worse as we head to the 'Moving Day'. The cracks have started to open up and Ireland have to dance on Bangladesh's tune a bit more tomorrow. Join us for the all-important day at 3.30 am GMT. You can join us earlier for the build up. Until then, cheers!

Despite losing wickets in heaps, Bangladesh ended with a healthy first innings total of 476, and all eyes were on the Irish batters as to how they would respond to their struggles with the bat. Andy Balbirnie and Paul Stirling started on a cautious note, adding 41 runs to the first wicket. The troubles began to bubble up once the spinners were introduced. Hasan Murad, with his slingy trajectory, troubled the Irish batters and picked 2 wickets while Taijul Islam and Mehidy Hasan Miraz ended with one each.

Bangladesh looked firmly in control as the scoreline read 433/5 with Litton Das and Mehidy Hasan Miraz well-set and marching towards the 500-mark goal. However, the tables turned once Ireland introduced Andy McBrine, as suddenly, Bangladesh found themselves reeling at 443/8 in the blink of an eye.

Well, everything is going against the plan for the visitors as they once again find themselves in a precarious position, but on the other side, Bangladesh will be over the moon with how Day 2 panned out. It started with Mushfiqur Rahim being stranded on 99 in his 100th Test match. The keeper-batter got the Dhaka crowd on its feet by raising his 13th Test century while Das played a silent warrior's role in helping him dearly.

From Sylhet to Dhaka, the story remains the same. Ireland once again struggle with the bat, having lost half of their side while still trailing by 378 runs. Not the first time in the series. It's an ongoing problem for Ireland to negotiate the spinners. Well, they have once again found it difficult to play them. Credit to the hosts for dominating not just the day but the overall game, and by extension, the series so far.

Taken at first slip, but no one from Bangladesh is convinced to go up for the review! Looped up, around off, Stephen Doheny tries to dig it out, but the ball beats him on the outside edge due to the turn. It clips the keeper's gloves and lobs towards Najmul Hossain Shanto at slip. An optimistic shout from the men around the bat, but it is turned down. That will be STUMPS on Day 2!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK! Bangladesh have found the opening they were searching for. Their pacers were a touch too straight early on and the Irish openers were quick to cash in. The shot from Paul Stirling was, to be honest, uncalled for, and he will be gutted with the choice he made. In the three overs of spin that we have seen so far, there haven’t been any alarms yet, and conditions still look good for batting. Cade Carmichael is in at number 3.

OUT! LBW! Huge appeal for LBW and up goes the finger of the umpire. Paul Stirling opts for the review. Khaled Ahmed bowls it fuller, on off and middle, with a little bit of inswing. Paul Stirling takes a couple of steps down the track to flick it away on the leg side, but the ball sneaks past the inner edge and thumps the front pad of the batter. The UltraEdge shows no bat involvement, and the Ball Tracking detects that the ball is hitting the leg pole. Ireland lose their first wicket and also their first review.
